verification_report.summary:
Both complete supplied sections were verified in textual order, with every new formula and limit checked under the stated conventions and granted internal inputs. No critical errors or gaps were found.

For isolated poles on a fibration, the common-norm orthonormal-basis argument proves the positive kernel difference, its exact total-variation mass, and the determinant comparison with the correct sign and q-dimensional scaling, including zero spaces. The strict integrability condition k+n>ma gives exactly max(floor(ma)-n+1,0), including integer thresholds. Section descent and product coordinates give the asserted global point-vanishing space; poles in one fiber impose a maximum. The quotient jet injection proves the O(m^(q-1)) codimension bound without surjectivity, including q=1 and n=q. The actual internal convergence and determinant statements apply on the Kähler base with its identity modification and the assumed positive-mass reference. Exact norm and probability-lift identities then prove all stated limits and the vanishing ambient normalization. The small-coefficient cutoff constructions and exact loss of fiber-position information are valid without BMP.

For the Hopf section, the ambient boundary index, projective monomial norms, binomial kernel, dimension formula and positive mass 1-a^q are correct. Chebyshev and dominated convergence establish total-variation convergence. The entropy estimates establish the potential limit, including t=a, uniformity near t=1 and eventual poles at t=0; fixed-curvature normalized compactness independently proves L1 convergence. The local potentials match values and first derivatives at the contact sphere, giving C1,1 gluing. Convolution and Bedford–Taylor continuity identify the determinant measure, with no interface mass; the non-pluripolar product removes the pole, also when q=1. The complex-line maximum principle proves envelope maximality. Analytic ideal domination and product-coordinate inequalities identify the entire upstairs competitor family without applying a closed-curvature theorem to the selecting weight. The Hopf fiber normalization gives precisely 1/(2n). Finally, the changed ideal type along the fiber and the nonempty open set distinguishing the raw selecting-weight Hermitian measure from the kernel limit are both justified.

The cited canonical book statements were read and their definitions, hypotheses and normalizations matched to each application.
